brief: William Blair downgrades NVDA to Market Perform after the Wall Street Journal reported Nvidia's board is preparing to remove CEO Jensen Huang. Huang acknowledged infidelity after the Financial Times reported a U.S. intelligence memo alleging a relationship with Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive U.S. intelligence believes China's Ministry of State Security recruited. The New York Times reported Megaspeed bought over $4.8B of Nvidia chips over two years, and a Commerce Department probe into suspected chip diversion to China moved to the Department of Justice after Nvidia's counsel contacted investigators. William Blair expects this to raise the odds of tighter export licensing and country caps, and names CFO Colette Kress, Ian Buck, and Jonathan Ross as internal succession candidates. Separately, the firm argues Nvidia's moat is narrowing: Google's TPU and AMD's Helios racks are winning share, and CUDA's porting-cost edge is eroding as frameworks and coding agents cut rewrite time, citing Anthropic's claim of porting to AMD's MI355X in three days. NVDA fell 9% after hours, 7% this week, and 27% off its October highs, now near a record-low 10x 2027 EPS. The firm still sees Nvidia's AI leadership intact but expects rotation toward AI names with less governance risk.
